source_text:
In Ruth
ΡΟΥΘ.
12.989 Καὶ ὄνομα τῇ δευτέρᾳ Ῥούθ. Ῥοὺθ τύπον φέρει τῶν ἐθνῶν· ἥτις κατέλιπε τὰ
πάτρια, καὶ ἡνώθη τῇ Ἰσραηλιτικῇ ἕξει. Ζητητέον δὲ πῶς, τοῦ νόμου ἀπαγορεύοντος
μὴ εἰσελθεῖν Μοαβίτην εἰς Ἐκκλησίαν Θεοῦ, ἡ Ῥοὺς Μοαβίτις οὖσα εἰσῆλθε. Καὶ
τοῦτο ζητῶν χρῆσαι τῷ· "∆ικαίω δὲ νόμος οὐ κεῖται, ἀλλὰ ἀδίκοις καὶ
ἀνυποτάκτοις."
thought_title: Ruth as type of the Gentiles and the law's non-application to the righteous
orientation: Origen is explaining the name of the second woman in the book of Ruth and resolving the legal difficulty of her entry into the assembly of God.
pass_a_gloss: And the name of the second was Ruth. Ruth bears a type of the Gentiles; she who left behind the ancestral things, and was joined to the Israelite state. But it must be inquired how, the law forbidding a Moabite not to enter into the assembly of God, Ruth, being a Moabite, entered. And in inquiring into this, apply the saying: "But the law is not laid down for the righteous, but for the lawless and disobedient."

choices.why: Keeps the verbal force of φέρει (bears) with the glossary term 'type' for τύπον, preserving the idea that Ruth carries or presents a type.
ἕξις means a state, condition, or disposition; 'state' captures the settled way of life or condition of being Israelite, avoiding the more abstract 'disposition' or 'habit'.
rejected: to the Israelite way of life

choices.why: The verbal adjective conveys necessity or obligation; 'it must be inquired' preserves the impersonal gerundive force.
χρῆσαι is a middle imperative meaning 'use' or 'apply'; adding 'the saying' makes the object explicit in English since τῷ alone is elliptical.
ἀνυπότακτος means 'not subject to authority, insubordinate'; 'disobedient' is the standard rendering in this Pauline context and matches the contrast with 'righteous'.

bible_refs.note: Δικαίῳ δὲ νόμος οὐ κεῖται, ἀλλὰ ἀδίκοις καὶ ἀνυποτάκτοις

pass_b_english: The second was named Ruth. Ruth bears a type of the Gentiles, because she left her ancestral customs behind and was joined to the Israelite way of life. But it must be inquired how Ruth, who was a Moabite, entered the assembly of God when the law forbids a Moabite to enter the assembly of God. And inquiring into this, apply the saying: "The law is not laid down for the righteous, but for the unjust and disobedient" (1 Timothy 1:9).

last_rejected.quote: But it must be inquired how
last_rejected.why: Ζητητέον is impersonal 'it must be inquired' — this is actually correct. But checking: 'But it must be inquired how Ruth... entered' — the source has 'the law forbids a Moabite to enter the assembly of God, Ruth the Moabite being/existing entered.' The English 'when the law forbids' changes the logical structure slightly but meaning is preserved. Actually re-checking: no modality error here.
last_rejected.ruling: Reporter self-corrects: no modality error. 'When' for κατέλιπε/ἡνώθη context preserves meaning adequately.
